A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Assay2Mol study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendix A.1–A.9 are readable and support reliable comparison despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original CrossDocked molecule-generation and docking results, predicted hERG optimization outcomes, and appendix sensitivity, similarity, and relevance analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original computational results and adds evaluations of random ZINC molecules and a sequence-filtered Assay2Mol variant in Table 1.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 adds an experimental DeepSeekV3 variant that uses MMseqs2 to discard retrieved BioAssays whose proteins exceed 30% sequence identity to the query, then retrieves replacements. This is a limited procedural adaptation; the principal workflow and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds ZINC20 compounds as a comparison population alongside FDA-approved drugs and generated molecules. The CrossDocked target coverage, hERG optimization tasks, and appendix case studies are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the 'ZINC 30 atoms' random-sampling baseline. The displayed CVAE, AR, Pocket2Mol, TamGen, TargetDiff, and context-free LLM comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New controls introduce a 30% sequence-identity exclusion condition and evaluation of 100 randomly sampled ZINC20 molecules restricted to 30 heavy atoms. Existing benchmark splits and primary settings are retained. Newly documented docking and manual-review settings do not establish changes to those existing experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a related-protein leakage check and extends the molecule-size analysis with a random fixed-size ZINC control. The existing hyperparameter, context-relevance, molecular-similarity, and TFPI failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Repeated-run, seed, and statistical uncertainty reporting are unchanged. The same result summaries and distribution plots are retained, with no added confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds two result rows: ZINC has mean Vina Dock −7.855, and sequence-filtered DeepSeekV3 has −7.826, versus −7.861 for the retained unfiltered variant. These are additional conditions, not same-setting performance improvements. Existing table values, figure results, and hERG outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem definition and cosine-similarity/top-k formulation in Equation 1 are unchanged. Expanded descriptions of existing empirical metrics introduce no new theoretical results, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction changes 'new candidate molecules' to 'candidate molecules' and 'active molecules' to 'candidate active molecules,' modestly narrowing novelty and activity claims. The central workflow contribution and abstract claims about docking performance and synthetic accessibility are retained.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the sequence-filtered results as evidence of generalization and uses the ZINC results to make docking-size bias concrete. Section 6 also explicitly explains the tradeoff between retrieving practical, synthesizable molecules and exploring previously unknown chemical space.

D1.justification: Appendix A.7 newly specifies the original ligand center, a 20-angstrom docking box in each dimension, and exhaustiveness 32. v2 also documents manual relevance criteria and the single expert reviewer, explains existing metric calculations, and clarifies reuse of baseline-generated molecules. These are disclosures rather than demonstrated revisions to existing settings.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds CLAMP and work by Schoenmaker, Han, and Smit on BioAssay modeling or annotation. Additional references support the new controls, metric explanations, and limitations. Existing references receiving publication or bibliographic updates remain the same works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, expands metric explanations and related-work discussion, converts molecule-selection sub-bullets into prose, and renames two appendix headings. The overall section order and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and adjusts column widths; Table 4 expands its caption to identify the reviewer. Figures and prompt boxes reflow across pages, and printed page numbers are removed. All ten figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: The new sequence-filtering check and random-ZINC control improve scrutiny of the docking results, while the added docking parameters and manual-review details improve reproducibility. More explicit novelty and docking-bias qualifications also improve interpretation. These are useful, targeted gains; they do not resolve the computational evaluation's acknowledged limitations or uncertainty about LLM pretraining overlap.
